question: The medical authority may declare a candidate as Fit, Unfit or ___________.
No Government servant shall be granted leave of any kind for a continuous period exceeding ___________.
A Government servant whose date of birth is the first of a month shall retire from service on the afternoon of ___________ on attaining the age of sixty years.
Service Book of the Government servant should be maintained in ___________.
No deputation of Government servant out of India shall be sanctioned without the previous approval of the ___________.
'Fee' includes unearned income such as income from property, dividends and interest on securities.
Honorarium shall be paid to government servants for dealing with parliamentary questions.
Recovery of deduction from Income tax from the subsistence allowance of a Government servant requires written consent of the Government servant.
'Duty' includes joining time.

When a Government servant is formally appointed to hold full charge of the duties of a higher post in the same office and in the same line of promotion, in addition to his ordinary duties, he shall be allowed additional pay for performing the duties of the lower post.
Two advance increments were sanctioned in the time-scale of a post, by an authority competent to create the post, as reward for meritorious work. Give comments citing the relevant Fundamental Rules.
Define 'Lien'. What are the circumstances under which a Government servant who has acquired lien on a post retains the lien on that post?
Define 'Honorarium'. What are the guiding principles which should be kept in view by the Administrative Authorities in granting 'Honorarium' to a Government servant?
State the circumstances under which an appropriate authority can withhold permission to a Government servant seeking voluntary retirement under FR56 (k) and FR 56 (m)?
The date of birth so declared by the Government servant and accepted by the Appropriate Authority are subject to alteration under certain circumstances. What are they?
Travelling Allowance is not admissible to a Government servant for a journey to and from the examination centre in respect of departmental examinations.
A journey on transfer begins or ends at the actual residence of the Government servant.
A Government servant in transit from one post to another ranks in the grade to which the lower of the two posts would entitle him.
Daily Allowance is admissible for any period of casual leave or restricted holiday availed while on tour.
Travelling Allowance is not admissible to a Government servant who is summoned to give evidence in a criminal case in his official capacity as a Government servant.
What is meant by Permanent Travelling Allowance? What are the conditions for its admissibility? Briefly explain how is it different from Conveyance Allowance.
